Hi Anna — Priyom from Security. I wanted to be explicit about what we can deliver and any limitations so your team can assess adequacy for CuraHealth's control objectives. Below is an operational description we use with enterprise customers.

1) EU-only processing guarantee
- We can pin customer workloads to EU regions (currently Frankfurt and Amsterdam). All compute nodes and persistent volumes for pinned workloads remain in the selected region unless the customer requests cross-region replication.
- Control plane connections remain over TLS; metadata in the control plane is minimised and can be configured to use a private VPC peering arrangement for Dedicated/Private deployments.

2) SCCs and lawful transfers
- Redwood will execute the standard EU Commission SCCs for controller-processor flows (we provide a signed amendment attaching the SCCs).
- For certain backend subprocessors (CDN, logging aggregator) based outside the EU, we implement supplemental technical measures: encryption at rest with region-bound KMS keys, strict IP allowlists for management plane, and contractual subprocessors obligations.

3) Deletion evidence — what we can provide
- Deletion event report (JSON lines delivered as a signed artifact): {timestamp UTC, dataset_id, deletion_job_id, operator_alias, retention_policy_id, objects_targeted_count, objects_removed_count, sha256_digest_of_manifest}
- Audit trail entry mapping deletion_job_id -> storage operation ids and replication completion status for the pinned region.
- For Hosted customers we can provide an attestational package (signed PDF) summarising the deletion job and pointing to the internal job id; for Dedicated/Private customers we can also provide access to a read-only audit console extract or a time-limited export of relevant audit records.

Operational notes / limitations:
- We do not expose low-level raw storage blocks or internal log streams. The deletion artifact above is designed to be cryptographically reproducible (sha256 over the manifest) but we stop short of shipping raw logs.
- If you require independent re-computation of a hash over deleted objects we can discuss an on-site attestation exercise for Dedicated deployments.
- Typical turnaround to produce a signed deletion artifact is 48–72 hours following the deletion job completion; we can commit to SLA-ed faster delivery for enterprise contracts.

If this aligns with your needs, I can provide a template deletion report (redacted example) for you to validate with your compliance team.
